item.title: ‘We Measure Success by Performance and Longevity:’ A Conversation With Emerging Voices Winners CO Adaptive
item.description: Featured in our latest Studio Snapshot is Brooklyn-based architecture studio CO Adaptive, founded by Ruth Mandl and Bobby Johnston in 2011. The firm describes itself as an "unbuild, design, and build practice," offering a refreshing and much-needed commitment to reuse, repurpose, and maintain. In our conversation, they shared more about their efforts toward circularity in architecture and construction, the value of collaboration, and how they strive to bring together design and craftsmanship. item.title: ‘Hideous’ and ‘vulgar’: White House ballroom vote delayed after avalanche of public criticism
item.description: A vote to progress the proposed controversial ballroom at the White House has been delayed due to public criticism of the plans. The National Capital Planning Commission pushed a vote on the project to next month after strong public backlash. item.title: Zaha Hadid Architects has the right to change its name, court rules
item.description: The UK Court of Appeal has ruled that Zaha Hadid Architects is not bound to its name, and that it does not need to perpetually pay royalties to the Zaha Hadid Foundation. The case centered on a trademark licence agreement signed in 2013, which allowed Zaha Hadid Limited, the architectural practice founded by the late architect, to use the “Zaha Hadid” name worldwide in exchange for a royalty payment of 6% of annual net income.
